profile.statistic: R-hat, the potential scale reduction factor — the between/within-chain convergence diagnostic of an iterative simulation, published under three names in the same literature (R-hat, PSRF, the Gelman-Rubin statistic)
profile.deriving_document: Gelman, A., Carlin, J. B., Stern, H. S., Dunson, D. B., Vehtari, A. & Rubin, D. B., 'Bayesian Data Analysis', 3rd ed. (2013), section 11.5 'Stopping the simulations', read at source 2026-08-05 in the authors' free electronic edition: 'We recommend computing the potential scale reduction for all scalar estimands of interest; if R-hat is not near 1 for all of them, continue the simulation runs (perhaps altering the simulation algorithm itself to make the simulations more efficient, as described in the next section). The condition of R-hat being ‘near’ 1 depends on the problem at hand, but we generally have been satisfied with setting 1.1 as a threshold.' The number is a reading stated inside a textbook section and hedged in the same sentence; the same book applies it as a criterion in its own worked examples ('R-hat < 1.1 for all parameters').
